title: Jonah and the Oath Revisited
premise: Petra Hartwell, an exiled storm-caller hiding as a charm-seller in the magic-forbidden city of Vessengard, is found by Wren, a mute child who speaks the First Tongue in dreams and carries a shard of dragon-fire in her chest. The shard is the last ember of the Oath that once bound the mortal realm to the dragon-realm of Ashfall, and its dying light is unraveling Petra's buried memories of who betrayed him into exile. Pursued by the Hollow Wardens who enforce the magic ban, Petra and Wren gather the scattered oath-keepers—a disgraced archivist, a river-witch, and Petra's estranged former apprentice—while learning that Wren is the Oath reborn in human form. At the ruined Gate of Ashfall, Petra must choose between restoring his stolen memories and spending them as fuel to reforge the covenant; he chooses the covenant, sacrificing his past so the dragon-fire burns again. The story ends with Petra nameless but not alone, raising Wren in a city where magic is slowly, warily returning, and with the first dragon in a century circling overhead.
about_author: J. M. Quintana is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping river deltas before turning to fantasy. They write about exile, memory, and the families we build from strangers, usually near water.

chapters.title: Charms for the Fearful
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. In rain-slick Vessengard, Petra sells harmless luck-charms while suppressing the storm that answers his moods. A routine day establishes his loneliness, his fear of discovery, and the Hollow Wardens patrolling for magic. Emotional beat: the ache of self-erasure—Petra has shrunk his life to survive it.

chapters.title: The Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. On the night of a dead-calm storm, a barefoot girl appears at his shop, and in his dreams she speaks a language older than any kingdom. She carries no shadow. Petra recognizes the First Tongue and knows exposure is certain if he keeps her. Emotional beat: terror warring with a pull he cannot name.

chapters.title: What the Wardens Burn
chapters.summary: Wren's POV (fragmentary, dreamlike). Wren remembers fire, a gate, and a voice calling her 'little ember.' Wardens raid the charm-shop; Petra's suppressed magic flares and levels the street. They flee into the undercity. Emotional beat: first rupture—Petra's hidden self breaks loose and cannot be hidden again.

chapters.title: The Archivist of Banned Things
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. In the flooded archive beneath the city, they find Odelia Vance, a disgraced archivist who catalogs forbidden histories. She identifies Wren's shard as dragon-fire—the last ember of the Oath between realms. Emotional beat: cautious hope; the first hint that Wren is not a victim but a key.

chapters.title: Memories in the Walls
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Odelia's archive holds records of Petra's trial and exile—but pages concerning his betrayal are scorched blank. Petra realizes his memories were taken, not lost. Wren's shard reacts to him, showing flashes: a tower, a friend's voice, a choice. Emotional beat: dread of one's own past.

chapters.title: The Hollow Warden's Bargain
chapters.summary: Warden-Sergeant Ilva's POV. Ilva, who led the raid, is revealed to be an oath-keeper's daughter working from inside the Wardens. She warns Petra that High Warden Corvess knows about Wren and wants the ember to seal the realms forever. Emotional beat: an enemy becomes an uneasy ally.

chapters.title: Downriver to Marrowfen
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The group escapes the city by barge with Ilva's forged papers. On the river, Wren begins speaking aloud in the First Tongue, and Petra understands her: she is afraid of burning out. Emotional beat: tenderness; the found family starts to form around a frightened child.

chapters.title: The River-Witch's Toll
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. In Marrowfen they seek Sable Yew, a river-witch and one of three living oath-keepers. Sable agrees to help but demands a toll: one true memory, freely given. Petra pays a small one—and feels the emptiness grow. Emotional beat: the cost of the quest made literal.

chapters.title: The Apprentice Who Waited
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Petra's estranged former apprentice Tamsin finds them, bitter: Petra vanished five years ago mid-lesson, memory already fraying, and Tamsin was left to face the Wardens alone. She refuses to help. Emotional beat: guilt; the quest's collateral damage has a face.

chapters.title: Ashfall in Dreams
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren dreams fully into Ashfall, the dragon-realm, and meets the dying dragon Vess who guards the guttering Gate. Vess shows her the Oath's making and the betrayal that broke it—a human oath-keeper who stole the ember's twin. Emotional beat: awe and grief; the scale of what was lost.

chapters.title: Corvess Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Ilva's POV. High Warden Corvess, revealed to be the ancient oath-breaker wearing a Warden's body, declares martial law and offers a bounty for the 'ember-child.' Ilva's cover frays. Emotional beat: the antagonist's true scope revealed—this is a war, not a manhunt.

chapters.title: The Scorch-Blank Page
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Sable reads the residue on Petra's scorched memories and recoils: the betrayal was Petra's own. He stole the ember's twin to save someone, then had the memory taken as punishment. Emotional beat: identity crisis—Petra must decide whether he is the story's hero or its villain.

chapters.title: What I Did to Save You
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Odelia reconstructs the truth: five years ago Petra stole the twin ember to keep the Gate from being sealed by the Wardens' founders, was caught, and chose memory-loss over revealing Wren's future existence—because Wren is the Oath reborn, and he had already met her, once, at the Gate. Emotional beat: devastating clarity; his exile was a sacrifice, not a sentence.

chapters.title: Tamsin's Choice
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin, tracking them for the bounty, corners Petra—and instead burns her own Warden credentials, choosing him. She reveals Corvess has Odelia captive. Emotional beat: reconciliation; the found family absorbs its angriest member.

chapters.title: Raid on the Black Archive
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. A rescue of Odelia goes wrong when Corvess springs his trap: he wants Petra to lead him to the Gate. Ilva is gravely wounded covering the escape. Odelia is saved but the archive burns. Emotional beat: fury and grief; the cost of resistance becomes real and personal.

chapters.title: The Ember's Hunger
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren's shard begins consuming her warmth to stay lit; she is dying as the Oath dies. She hides it, then confesses to Petra in the First Tongue. Petra understands every word now—the language is returning to him as his memories burn away. Emotional beat: quiet horror and fierce protectiveness.

chapters.title: March to the Gate
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The company crosses the Ashfall wastes—Petra, Wren, Tamsin, Odelia, and the convalescing Ilva—pursued by Corvess and a Warden legion. Petra's storm-calling returns fully, wild and costly. Emotional beat: resolve; the scattered keepers become a single, deliberate company.

chapters.title: The Gate of Ashfall
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. They reach the Gate and the dying dragon Vess. The reforging requires an oath-keeper to feed the ember with what they value most. Corvess arrives, offering Petra his stolen memories in exchange for walking away. Emotional beat: the temptation of the self.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Climax. Petra feeds the ember his memories—every one, not just the stolen ones—and speaks the First Tongue to seal the new Oath. Corvess, denied his prize, tries to seize the Gate and is unmade by dragon-fire as the realms reopen. Wren blazes and survives, the Oath whole. Emotional beat: transcendence through sacrifice.

chapters.title: A Man With No Yesterday
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Petra wakes nameless, remembering nothing—but his hands still know charm-work, and Wren still knows him. Tamsin, Odelia, and Ilva vow to be his memory. Emotional beat: grief braided with grace; identity handed to others to hold.

chapters.title: First Flight
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In a Vessengard where magic is cautiously legal again, Wren—now Petra's ward—watches the first dragon in a century cross the sky. She teaches Petra his own name, which she kept safe for him. Emotional beat: homecoming; memory survives in the ones who love us.

chapters.title: The Oath Revisited
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Epilogue. Petra, relearning himself through the family that chose him, reopens his charm-shop—now selling small true magic. At closing time, a knock: a stranger with ember-bright eyes, the first of many from Ashfall. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope; the story ends where it began, with a knock at the door.
